title: A Short Training Session
instructions: Listen carefully. Choose the option that best matches what is said or implied.

audio.description: Colleagues plan a practical training session around busy hours.

transcript.text: The new booking system starts next month. We need to train everyone, but a full-day session would leave the front desk short-staffed.
Could we run two shorter sessions, before opening and after lunch? People can choose by shift. We should record a demo for anyone absent.
That sounds practical. A recording can cover common tasks, but cannot answer unusual questions. We will need support afterwards.
I can answer questions the first week. Let’s list issues so we can improve the guide instead of repeating answers.
I will send choices today. Reply by Friday so we know how many places are needed. Anyone missing both sessions can watch the recording.

questions.prompt: Why do they avoid a full-day training session?
options: The booking system is not ready.
It would leave the front desk short-staffed.
The team does not want a recording.
questions.explanation: Colleague A says a full-day session would leave the front desk short-staffed.

questions.prompt: How will they make the training fit different shifts?
options: Repeat the same full-day session every week
Ask everyone to work an extra shift
Offer two shorter sessions at different times
questions.explanation: Colleague B proposes a session before opening and another after lunch.

questions.prompt: What limitation do they see in a recorded demonstration?
options: It will be too long to watch.
It cannot respond to unusual questions.
It will only work at the front desk.
questions.explanation: Colleague A says the recording can cover common tasks but cannot answer questions about unusual bookings.

questions.prompt: Why will they keep a shared list of problems?
options: To improve the guide and avoid repeating answers
To decide who should miss training
To remove unusual bookings from the system
To measure how quickly people work
questions.explanation: Colleague B says the list will help update the guide instead of answering the same questions repeatedly.
